sections.skill: Interpret APR and convert it to monthly and daily periodic rates

questions.prompt: A loan has an APR of 18%. If interest is charged monthly, what is the monthly periodic rate?
questions.intro: APR (annual percentage rate) is the yearly cost of credit, including the interest rate and certain fees, expressed as a percent. Lenders often charge interest each month using a periodic rate: monthly periodic rate = APR ÷ 12.

misconceptions.C: Confuses APR with a monthly rate

sources: CFPB (Truth in Lending, Regulation Z): Lenders must disclose the APR and finance charge; APR expresses the yearly cost of credit, including certain fees. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/)

questions.prompt: A credit card has a 21.9% APR and charges interest daily. What is the daily periodic rate (use 365 days; nearest thousandth of a percent)?
questions.intro: Many credit cards use a daily periodic rate = APR ÷ 365 (some use 360). Interest is figured each day on the balance.

misconceptions.D: Confuses APR with a daily rate

sources: CFPB (Truth in Lending, Regulation Z): Lenders must disclose the APR and finance charge; APR expresses the yearly cost of credit, including certain fees. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/)

questions.prompt: Two $5,000 loans for one year: Loan A has a 9% interest rate plus a $150 fee; Loan B has a 10% interest rate and no fee. Which has the lower total cost?
questions.intro: Comparing loans by interest rate alone can mislead, because fees add to the cost. APR includes the interest rate and certain fees, which makes it the better number for comparing loans of the same term.

sections.skill: APR versus APY and effective cost

questions.prompt: A loan charges 1.5% per month, compounded monthly. What is the effective annual rate (nearest tenth of a percent)?
questions.intro: APR is a simple yearly rate: monthly rate × 12. If interest is added each month and then charged interest, the effective annual rate (like APY for savings) is higher: (1 + monthly rate)^12 − 1.
sources: CFPB (Truth in Lending, Regulation Z): Lenders must disclose the APR and finance charge; APR expresses the yearly cost of credit, including certain fees. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/)

questions.prompt: Savings accounts advertise APY, while loans advertise APR. Why might a lender prefer to advertise APR?

choices.text: APR is always higher than APY
APR includes all possible fees, making it look higher
APR leaves out compounding, so it looks lower
APR is used only for savings

questions.correct_answer: APR leaves out compounding, so it looks lower
questions.intro: For the same compounding, APY (or the effective annual rate) is higher than APR whenever interest compounds more than once a year. Federal rules require savings to show APY and loans to show APR.
questions.feedback: The effective cost with compounding is higher than the stated APR.
sources: CFPB (Truth in Lending, Regulation Z): Lenders must disclose the APR and finance charge; APR expresses the yearly cost of credit, including certain fees. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/)

questions.prompt: A credit card has a 24% APR with daily compounding. Is the effective annual rate higher or lower than 24%?

choices.text: It depends on the credit limit

questions.intro: With compounding, interest is charged on interest already added. The effective annual rate = (1 + APR ÷ n)^n − 1, where n is the number of compounding periods in a year.
questions.feedback: Compounding makes the effective rate a bit above 24% (about 27%).
sources: CFPB (Truth in Lending, Regulation Z): Lenders must disclose the APR and finance charge; APR expresses the yearly cost of credit, including certain fees. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/)

questions.prompt: Which number should Ali use to compare two personal loans with the same term but different fees?

choices.text: Only the monthly payment, ignoring the term

questions.intro: The APR of a loan includes the interest rate and certain fees, so loans with the same term can be compared by APR.
questions.feedback: For loans of the same term, APR captures both rate and certain fees.
sources: CFPB (Truth in Lending, Regulation Z): Lenders must disclose the APR and finance charge; APR expresses the yearly cost of credit, including certain fees. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/)

questions.prompt: A $1,000 loan for one year has a $50 fee and charges 5% interest. Roughly what is its APR?
questions.intro: APR for a simple one-year loan ≈ (interest + fees) ÷ amount borrowed × 100.

misconceptions.D: Uses the fee as a percent

sources: CFPB (Truth in Lending, Regulation Z): Lenders must disclose the APR and finance charge; APR expresses the yearly cost of credit, including certain fees. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/)

questions.prompt: A Truth in Lending disclosure shows: Amount financed $8,000; Finance charge $1,620; Total of payments $9,620. What is the finance charge?

choices.text: The full amount of money borrowed: $8,000
The dollar cost of the credit: $1,620

questions.correct_answer: The dollar cost of the credit: $1,620
questions.intro: The Truth in Lending Act requires lenders to show key terms before you sign: the APR, the finance charge (the dollar cost of credit), the amount financed, and the total of payments.
questions.feedback: The finance charge is the total dollar cost of credit.
sources: CFPB (Truth in Lending, Regulation Z): Lenders must disclose the APR and finance charge; APR expresses the yearly cost of credit, including certain fees. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/)

questions.prompt: A loan disclosure shows: Amount financed $8,000; Total of payments $9,620; 48 monthly payments. What is each payment (nearest cent)?
questions.intro: When payments are equal, each payment = total of payments ÷ number of payments.
sources: CFPB (Truth in Lending, Regulation Z): Lenders must disclose the APR and finance charge; APR expresses the yearly cost of credit, including certain fees. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/)

questions.prompt: Amount financed $8,000; finance charge $1,620. The finance charge is what percent of the amount financed (nearest tenth)?
questions.intro: Comparing the finance charge with the amount financed shows how much the credit costs relative to the amount borrowed.
questions.feedback: $1,620 ÷ $8,000 = 0.2025 → 20.3% of the amount borrowed, spread over 4 years.

misconceptions.B: Divides by the total of payments

questions.prompt: Why must lenders give this disclosure BEFORE you sign?

choices.text: So you can compare offers and understand the cost
So the lender can raise the rate later without telling you
Because the IRS requires it for taxes
So you can skip reading the contract

questions.correct_answer: So you can compare offers and understand the cost
questions.intro: Federal law (the Truth in Lending Act) requires the disclosure so borrowers see the cost of credit in a standard form.
questions.feedback: Standard disclosures make costs comparable across lenders.
sources: CFPB (Truth in Lending, Regulation Z): Lenders must disclose the APR and finance charge; APR expresses the yearly cost of credit, including certain fees. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/)

questions.prompt: Which disclosure item is the best single number for comparing loans with the same term?
questions.intro: A Truth in Lending disclosure lists the APR, finance charge, amount financed, total of payments, and payment schedule.
questions.feedback: APR summarizes the yearly cost of credit.

misconceptions.A: Payment depends on amount and term, not just the cost of credit
misconceptions.D: Depends on the amount borrowed, so it misleads across loan sizes
